name: presentation

frames.best_why: The full cream slide, its three columns and the whole numbered thumbnail rail are visible together.

tagline: A deck viewer with a thumbnail rail and one large, zoomable slide.
summary: A .pptx viewer: a numbered thumbnail rail down the left, a large auto-fitted slide on the right, and in-slide selection with resize and rotate handles. Clicking a thumbnail flips the deck.
appearance: A bordered app panel with a thin toolbar and a file picker. Down the left runs a column of small numbered slide previews; the rest is a large framed slide canvas showing cream pages with serif headlines and thin rules, or dark green cover slides.
behaviour: Clicking a thumbnail swaps the big slide and the viewport refits it to the space. Inside a slide, objects can be marquee-selected, dragged, resized and rotated with handles; on narrow screens the rail slides out from behind a toggle button.
demo_content: A listening-room deck: "After the needle drops." plus a page on control, settle and quiet.
search_phrases: powerpoint deck viewer in the browser
slide thumbnails beside a large page
browse a pptx file with a side rail
view and select items on a slide
slide editor panel for a web app
open a pptx and flip through pages
how to render powerpoint slides on a website
use_when: Users need to open and page through a real .pptx deck inside the app, optionally editing slide objects.
avoid_when: It leans on a separate .pptx parser, needs a container with real height, and shows nothing until a deck loads.
customise: Give the provider a store loaded from a .pptx buffer, then compose the thumbnail list, content, viewport and slide. Every part takes a className and replacement children.
weight_why: Parses a .pptx file and renders every slide plus a thumbnail for each, so cost grows with deck size.

a11y.note: Thumbnails take focus and the mobile rail has labels, but slide object keyboard support comes from the underlying package and nothing checks reduced motion.

issues: Frames 1 and 2 show the cover slide with body copy so dim against the green that it is barely readable.
The demo loads a deck from one fixed remote URL and swallows failures, leaving an empty panel if it changes.
polish_why: Crisp editorial slides and a tidy rail; the dim cover body text is hard to read.
